target_customer: Engineering and security teams at companies handling sensitive customer data under SOC 2, HIPAA or GDPR programs
problem: Sensitive fields in databases and APIs are readable by too many people and applications, and encryption at rest is too blunt to control access per property.
business_model: B2B software deployed inside the customer's own infrastructure, sold as a data security platform
product_category: Data security and field-level access control

founders.name: Ryan Cooke
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page; background not found in sources checked.

competitors.name: Skyflow
competitors.what: Data privacy vault that isolates sensitive data behind an API with tokenization and residency controls

technical_complexity.rationale: A proxy that discovers sensitive properties and enforces policy between apps and databases across many database types is standard infrastructure engineering with hard integration parts, built by a one or two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Deployment inside customer infrastructure creates some integration stickiness, but a crowded data security field with funded vault, proxy and governance vendors made the wedge copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded data security vendors already covered adjacent ground. The company was acquired by WorkOS, reported as January 2024, rather than copied.

market_need_then: Compliance programs such as SOC 2, HIPAA and GDPR pushed companies to restrict access to PII, and the company's own pitch cited customer PII exposure and production access as common pain points.

branding.domain_note: Used jumpwire.io, not an exact .com; the site did not resolve when fetched in 2026.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and compliance oriented in the YC description

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand pages found beyond the YC listing; a search for the name returned unrelated Jump companies.

outcome_analysis: JumpWire was a one founder data security startup from Winter 2022 that was acquired by WorkOS, reported as January 2024, after about two years. The buyer needed data access governance next to its enterprise identity products, so the exit looks like a small tuck in deal. No price, funding history or post-mortem is public, so the story beyond the acquisition cannot be told.
notes: The acquirer and January 2024 date come from the YC page (WorkOS, 2024) plus two aggregator profiles of WorkOS; no WorkOS or JumpWire press release was found. Unverified: one aggregator (VCBacked) lists about 500K dollars of pre-seed funding with Y Combinator as investor; not recorded as a round. Company website did not resolve (dead or moved). Competition list holds only one source dated near the batch; Immuta and Satori coverage found was not clearly dated to the founding window.
